# read_C — pp. 33–35 (leaves n34–n36), established from the images

Line counts: p. 33 has five lines (leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔), p. 34 five lines, p. 35 five lines (leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔).
The witness's line breaks match the print on all three pages (15/15 lines).
The part ends at 35.5 …གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔. The rest of that line (དེ་ནས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་) begins the next part. It is transcribed in full, as asked.
Each line was cropped in quarters at ×3.3 and every doubtful syllable at ×6–×14.

## The image overruled the witness (23)

| page.line | witness → print | why |
|---|---|---|
| 33.1 | ཀྱང་གྱིས་ཆོག → ཀྱང་གིས་ཆོག | checked at ×9: there is no ya-btags under ག. Compare ཀྱཻ later in the same line, which has a clear subscript hook. The other recension has ངོ་ཤེས་པས་ཀྱང་ཆོག (see the misprints section) |
| 33.1 | རང་སྟན་དུ → རང་སྣང་དུ | the stack is ས over ན (not ཏ), and the final is ང (not ན). Same word as at the start of the line |
| 33.5 | ཐོམས་ཅད → ཐམས་ཅད | there is no na-ro over ཐ |
| 34.1 | བརྡལ་བaའི → བརྡལ་བའི | stray latin letter in the witness |
| 34.1 | བཅོས་ལྡན → བཅོམ་ལྡན | the final is clearly མ |
| 34.2 | མདོག་ཀར་པོ → མདོག་དཀར་པོ | a prefix ད is clearly there |
| 34.2 | སེདྒེའི → སེངྒེའི | the base is ང with a subjoined ག (one stack, as at 18.1 in the print) |
| 34.2 | འཁོར་རྩིབས → འཁོར་ལོ་རྩིབས | checked at ×9: ལོ (la with na-ro) stands between འཁོར and རྩིབས. The witness dropped a syllable. The other recension has the same, འཁོར་ལོ་རྩིབས |
| 34.2 | ཡུམ་ནམ་ཁའི → ཡུམ་ནམཁའི | contraction: ན, མ, ཁ run together with no tsheg (×7). There is only one མ. Needs `# fix` |
| 34.2 | (line end) དབིངས་ → དབྱིངྶ་ | the ya-btags under བ is clear. The final ས is written small under the foot of ང (ང + subjoined ས U+0FB6), a line-end abbreviation of the same kind as གྶི at 20.4. Needs `# fix` |
| 34.3 | འོང་ངོ་༔ → འོང་ངོ༔ | there is no tsheg between ངོ and ༔ (×6) |
| 34.3 | ཕྱུང་པོ → ཕུང་པོ | there is no ya-btags under ཕ |
| 34.4 | རྣམས་པར → རྣམ་པར | there is no ས after རྣམ |
| 34.4 | སྣང་མཛོད → སྣང་མཛད | the mark above ཛ is the letter's own tsa-phru hook, not a na-ro. There is no vowel |
| 34.5 | འོང་ངོ་༔ → འོང་ངོ༔ | there is no tsheg before ༔ |
| 34.5 | (line end) འོངོ་༔ → འོངོ༔ | contraction འོངོ, as printed (one ང, ×10). There is no tsheg before ༔. Needs `# fix` |
| 35.1 | ལྡན་པོ་ཆོས → ལྡན་པ་ཆོས | there is no na-ro on པ. The na-ro next to it belongs to ཆོས |
| 35.2 | བྲོས་ཤིང་༔ → བྲོས་ཤིང༔ | there is no tsheg before ༔ |

| 35.5 | སྣང་མཛོད → སྣང་མཛད | the same as 34.4: the mark is the tsa-phru, not a vowel |
| 35.5 | ཐུགས་རྫེའི → ཐུགས་རྗེའི | the base is ཇ (×8). Compare རྗེ at the top of p. 36 |
| 35.5 | མོས་པ་གྱིས → མོས་བ་གྱིས | the letter is the closed བ (×10). Compare the open པ of པའི in the same line. This is the print's habit (see 33.3 གདམས་བའི, 33.4 སྙམ་བའི), so it is kept |

Witness readings checked and confirmed, though they look odd: 33.3 གདམས་བའི and 33.4 སྙམ་བའི (both have བ), 33.4 བསངས, 33.2 བསྒོམ་སྒྲུབ, 33.3 and 33.2 དངངས, 34.1 ནཾ་མཁའ (see fixes), 34.4 སྐྲག and མཆོར, 34.5 སྐྲག་མེད, 35.1 ལས་ངན་གྱིས, 35.3 མ་བཀྲག་པར.

## [?]

None. Every syllable could be read at ×6 or more.

Two places are close calls but are not marked [?]:
- 35.1 (line end) ཁྱོད་ and 35.5 (line end) ལྡན་: a row of three filler dots follows the last letter, and the tsheg can't be told apart from the first filler dot. I kept the witness's tsheg. The fillers themselves are left out, following the read_A rule.
- 34.2 དབྱིངྶ: the small ས under ང is clear in shape. It sits just above the next line's head-line, but it is not part of that line.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

```
# fix: ནཾ => ནམ
# fix: ནམཁའི => ནམ་མཁའི
# fix: དབྱིངྶ => དབྱིངས
# fix: འོངོ => འོང་ངོ
# fix: ཁྱོདའོད => ཁྱོད་འོད
```
- 34.1 ནཾ་མཁའ (line start): ན with anusvara stands for ནམ. This is the same kind of abbreviation as པའཾ/ལཾ, but here it is at the start of the line.
- 34.2 ནམཁའི: a contraction, like ནམཁའ at 20.5.
- 34.2 (line end) དབྱིངྶ: a line-end abbreviation.
- 34.5 (line end) འོངོ༔: a contraction. It is the same phrase as འོང་ངོ༔ earlier in the same line.
- 35.2→35.3: there is no tsheg after ཁྱོད at the line end (the next line starts with འོད).

## Suspected misprints (kept as printed)

1. 34.5 ལྷའི་འོད་དཀར་པོ་སྐྲག་མེད → བཀྲག་མེད. Certainty is high. "The dull white light of the gods" is the same phrase that the print itself writes ལྷའི་འོད་དཀར་པོ་བཀྲག་མེད at 35.2. The other recension has བཀྲག་མེད. Reading སྐྲག་མེད ("fearless") makes no sense here. Proposed: `# fix: སྐྲག་མེད => བཀྲག་མེད` (34.5 only, because 35.2 is already correct).
2. 35.3 མ་བཀྲག་པར → མ་སྐྲག་པར. Certainty is high. The sentence is "do not be terrified, do not fear (མ་སྐྲག་པར)…". The other recension has མ་སྔངས་ཤིག་མ་སྐྲག་པར. Reading "not lustrous" makes no sense. The print has swapped སྐྲག and བཀྲག here and at item 1. Proposed: `# fix: མ་བཀྲག་པར => མ་སྐྲག་པར`.
3. 34.4 གསལ་ལ་དྭངས་པ༔ སྐྲག་ལ་མཆོར་བ་གཅིག → probably བཀྲག་ལ་… Certainty is moderate to high. The light is described as clear, bright and lustrous. The other recension has བཀྲག་ལ་འཚེར་བ, and the print's own 35.3 has གསལ་ལ་འཚེར་བ་དྭངས་ལ་བཀྲག་ཆེ་བ. The letters སྐྲ are certain on the image. If the fix is made: `# fix: སྐྲག་ལ་མཆོར => བཀྲག་ལ་མཆོར`. The second word, མཆོར་བ (the letters are certain, ×10), is not a clear misprint. mchor ba ("beautiful, splendid") is a real word, though the other recension has འཚེར་བ ("glittering"). Leave it.
4. 35.1 ལས་ངན་གྱིས་དབང་གིས, probably meant as ལས་ངན་གྱི་དབང་གིས ("by the power of bad karma"). The other recension has གྱི. Certainty is moderate: the doubled instrumental is ungrammatical, but slips like this are common. The print's own habit (it writes གཅིག་གི for གིས) runs the other way. Possible `# fix: ངན་གྱིས་དབང => ངན་གྱི་དབང`. This one is the drafter's choice.
5. 33.1 ངོ་ཤེས་པ་ཀྱང་གིས་ཆོག: the letters are certain. The other recension has ངོ་ཤེས་པས་ཀྱང་ཆོག ("it is enough just to recognise [it]"). The print's ཤེས་པ་ཀྱང་ཆོག with an extra གིས can be read as "…recognising, by that alone, suffices". It is awkward, but it cannot be corrected in only one way (པ་ཀྱང་གིས, or ཤེས་པས་ཀྱང). It is not a clear misprint. Note only.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: བ for པ after open syllables (33.3 གདམས་བའི, 33.4 སྙམ་བའི, 35.5 མོས་བ); 33.2/33.3/35.3 དངངས for སྔངས; 33.5 སྐུ་རུ; 34.1/34.3/34.4/35.1/35.3 མཐིང་ཁ for མཐིང་ག.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- 33.3: the print repeats ན (…མ་ཤེས་ན་སྒྲ་འོད་ཟེར་གསུམ་ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན་འཁོར་བར་འཁྱམ་མོ, "if… if you do not recognise the three, you wander in saṃsāra"). The other recension has ངོ་མ་ཤེས་པས ("because you do not recognise"). Little difference.
- 33.3: print གདམས་བའི་གནས ("the point/place of the instruction"); other recension གདམ་པའི་གནད ("the key point"). Close in sense.
- 33.4: print བརྒྱལ་ནས་འགྲོ་སྟེ; other recension ཤེས་པ་བརྒྱལ་འགྲོ་སྟེ. Same sense.
- 34.1: print ནམ་མཁའ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཁ་དོག་མཐིང་ཁར་འཆར་རོ; other recension …འོད་དང་ཁ་དོག་མཐིང་གར. The print leaves out "light".
- 34.1: print ཐིག་ལེ་བརྡལ་བའི་ཞིང་ཁམས་ནས; other recension adds མཐིང་ཀ ("the blue realm").
- 34.3: print གནས་སུ་དག་པ༔ (a statement); other recension དག་པས (causal: "because the aggregate is purified…").
- 34.4: print སྐྲག་ལ་མཆོར་བ (see misprints); other recension བཀྲག་ལ་འཚེར་བ.
- 34.5: print མིག་གིས་མི་བཟོད་པ; other recension མིག་གིས་ལྟ་མི་བཟོད་པ ("unbearable to look at"). Same sense.
- 34.5: print …ཀྱང་མདུན་དུ་ཟུག་ནས་འོངོ ("also comes piercing before you"). Other recension …ཀྱང་མདུན་དུ་འོད་དང་གཤིབ་མར་འཆར་རོ ("dawns alongside the [blue] light"). The verb and image differ.
- 35.2: print ཁྱོད་དགའ་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ནས་འོང་གི; other recension …འདུ་ཤེས་སྐྱེས་ནས. The print has no verb ("a thought of delight [arising]").
- 35.3: print …མ་དངངས་ཤིག༔ མ་བཀྲག་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི…; other recension …མ་སྔངས་ཤིག་མ་སྐྲག་པར༔ དེ་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི…. The print has no དེ་ནི.
- 35.4: print ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཡིན་ནོ (a closed statement); other recension ཡིན་གྱི (connective).
- 35.5: print རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ཀྱི་ཐུགས་རྗེའི; other recension རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ཡབ་ཡུམ་གྱི. The print has no "father-mother". Also, the print runs ཡིན་ནོ་སྐྱབས་སུ with a tsheg where the other recension has ༔.
